title: Fog of war
idea: Npcs see a circle around them; everything else on the map is under a black veil, solid where never discovered and half see-through where discovered but out of sight (issue 6).

glossary.meaning: The circle around an npc's feet, 500 map px in radius, that has sight. Nothing blocks it.
Inside the view field of an npc on your team: the current state shows, with no veil.
The black layer drawn over the map wherever there is no sight.
No npc on your team has ever had sight here: the veil is solid and nothing shows.
An npc on your team had sight here before but none does now: the veil is 0.5 opacity over the snapshot.
The ground, trees and walls of a spot as they were when the team last had sight of it. It may be out of date.
A player and their allies. They share sight, discovered areas and snapshots.

features.name: View field
features.whatItDoes: Gives each npc a circle of sight around its feet.
details: The radius is 500 map px, one value that replaces the script sightRange.
Trees and walls do not block it.
All npcs on a team share what they see.
Only npcs give sight, not walls or other objects.

features.name: Veil
features.whatItDoes: Covers the map in black wherever the team has no sight.
details: Solid black where never discovered, 0.5 opacity where discovered.
No veil where there is sight.
Its edges are blocky, hard-edged square cells that match the pixel art.
The screen UI, such as the Terminal button and Terminal, draws over the veil.

features.name: Snapshot
features.whatItDoes: Keeps showing discovered areas as they looked when last seen.
details: Under the 0.5 veil, the ground, trees and walls show as last seen, even if they have since been cut, built or destroyed.
Npcs, arrows and dropped items do not show under the 0.5 veil.
A spot's snapshot updates as soon as the team has sight of it again.
Your own wall plans, crosses and path lines follow the same veil rules, so they can be hidden.

features.name: Script find
features.whatItDoes: Makes an npc script's find search what the team knows, instead of a range around the npc.
details: It searches live things in sight plus the snapshot of discovered areas.
Never-discovered areas return nothing.
Things that are not in snapshots, such as dropped items, are found only in sight.
If a found thing is gone on arrival, the snapshot has already updated and the next find picks something else.

features.name: Orders in the veil
features.whatItDoes: Lets mouse orders go anywhere, whatever the veil shows.
details: Npcs can be sent into dim or solid black.
Walls can be planned in dim or solid black.
Clicks hit what the screen shows: hidden things count as ground, and a tree or plan in the snapshot can be targeted.

features.name: Dev key
features.whatItDoes: A key toggles the veil off on screen for testing, like the existing dev view keys.
details: Sight, snapshots and script find keep working the same underneath.

flows.name: Scout the map
steps: The game starts with sight around the team's npcs and solid black everywhere else.
Send an npc into the black; the area inside its view field clears and shows the current state.
The npc walks on; the area it left stays discovered, at 0.5 opacity, showing the snapshot.
An npc returns; the veil clears and the snapshot updates to the current state.

examples.situation: A tree was seen, the npc left, and an enemy cut the tree down.
examples.whatHappens: The tree still shows under the 0.5 veil. Once sight returns, it disappears.

examples.situation: A script's find picks a remembered tree, and the npc arrives to find it gone.
examples.whatHappens: The snapshot updates as the spot comes into sight, so the next find picks something else.

examples.situation: An enemy npc walks through a discovered area with no sight on it.
examples.whatHappens: It does not show. Only the snapshot shows, under the 0.5 veil.

examples.situation: A wall is planned in solid black.
examples.whatHappens: The plan is made but does not show, and script find does not see it until an npc on the team has sight of it.

examples.situation: The only npc in an area dies.
examples.whatHappens: That area goes straight to discovered, at 0.5 opacity, with its snapshot.

leftOut: Sight blocked by trees or walls.
Sight from walls or other objects.

decisions.decision: A team's npcs, the player's and allies', share sight, discovered areas and snapshots.
The view field and script find share one setting: the view field radius is 1000 map px, and find no longer has a range limit.
Script find searches sight plus the discovered snapshot, so a found object might be gone on arrival; the next find then picks something else.
decisions.reason: The user said a discovered area is only a snapshot of that moment.

decisions.decision: Under the 0.5 veil, ground, trees and walls show as last seen; npcs, arrows and items do not show.
The veil's edges are blocky square cells with hard edges.
Mouse orders, walking and wall plans alike, can go anywhere, including into solid black.
Sight is a plain circle; trees and walls do not block it.
Your own wall plans, crosses and path lines follow the veil rules, and are not drawn over it.
A dev key toggles the veil off on screen; sight and find keep working underneath.
project.spec.json is the fog of war spec; the finished Terminal spec moved to docs/specs/terminal.spec.json.
Replaces D-2's radius: the view field radius is 500 map px.

assumptions.statement: The game has no teams yet, only a player index, so the screen shows P1's veil and each player is their own team until allies exist.
A veil cell is one tile, 10 map px.
The dev key is V, which is unused today.
Other players' scripts use their own team's knowledge through the same find rules.
